goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` (see the `+             :website_name,` line), directly contradicting the claim that it is not included and thus leaked to anonymous viewers when `website` is hidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so AMS never calls it and `website_name` is always in /users/:username.json (null when there is no website), unlike the other conditional keys.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` plus a conditional method `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In ActiveModel::Serializer-style conditional attribute hooks are typically named `include_<attr>?`; with the current name, the conditional is likely never consulted and `website_name` would be serialized regardless (nil when `website` is blank), contrary to the intended `website.present?` gating.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `websiteName` computed property removed from the controller and the template switched to `model.website_name`, which is newly provided by `UserSerializer#website_name`. However, the finding’s core claim references `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:210` and asserts that `save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response, causing `model.website_name` to be stale after edits. That `save()` code path is not shown/changed in this diff, and nothing in the diff demonstrates how the client updates the user model after a website edit, so the stated stale/null behavior cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

Core behavior in this PR appears consistent, but the removal could be a backward-compatibility concern for any external plugin/connector templates that referenced `{{websiteName}}`, since no shim/alias is added in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — website_name` is missing from `untrusted_attributes`, so it gets serialized for TL0 users viewed by anonymous even though `website` is suppressed; the template now keys on `model.website_name`, which re-exposes the hidden website (the anti-spam restriction is bypassed) and the TL0 spec does not check the new key

While the template does switch to `model.website_name`, the alleged omission from `untrusted_attributes` (and resulting exposure bypass) is not supported by the changes shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `def include_website_name` (no `?`) intended to gate serialization of the new `:website_name` attribute. In ActiveModel::Serializers/Discourse serializer patterns, conditional attribute inclusion hooks are typically `include_<attr>?`; as written, this method won’t be invoked for `website_name`, so the intended conditional inclusion is effectively dead and the attribute may be included unconditionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — Replacing the client computed `websiteName` with a server-computed `website_name` leaves it stale after the user edits their website in preferences (`User#save` only refreshes `bio_excerpt`), so the profile shows the old name, or a globe with an empty link after clearing the website, until a full reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `websiteName` removed from the client controller and the template switched to `model.website_name`, which is now serialized server-side with `include_website_name`. However, the claim about staleness after editing preferences depends on client-side save/refresh behavior (e.g., `User#save` only refreshing `bio_excerpt`) that is not shown anywhere in this diff, so the described broken behavior cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — URI()` raises InvalidURIError on URLs with spaces or non-ASCII (IDN) characters, and the `rescue nil` turns that into `website_name` nil, so the website disappears from the profile where the old `split("/")[2]` still showed the host

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the profile template to render the website block only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), and removes the prior JS `websiteName` computed from `model.website`. In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return `nil` on parsing errors (e.g., invalid/odd URLs), while `include_website_name` still includes the attribute whenever `website.present?`. That results in `website_name` being `nil`/`null` and the website section not rendering even though `model.website` exists, which is a behavior regression compared to the old `split("/")[2]` approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Host comparisons are case-sensitive (`URI#host` keeps case, so `http://Example.com/u` does not match `example.com`), so same-domain URLs with uppercase hosts fall back to showing the bare host

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the claim that `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the original case, making host comparisons case-sensitive and causing same-domain uppercase hosts to be treated as different. The diff shows no explicit downcasing, but it also does not show any evidence that `URI#host` keeps case; the code simply uses Ruby's URI parser. Since the alleged behavior is not demonstrated or verifiable from the diff itself, and the review comment asserts a specific library behavior not shown here, the finding is not grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — The equal-label-count branch treats any two hosts sharing everything after the first label as the same domain, e.g. `example.co.uk` vs `other.co.uk` or `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io`, and shows the full path for unrelated sites

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` and, if equal, returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. This treats any hosts that share everything after the first label as the same “domain” (e.g., `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io`, or `example.co.uk` vs `other.co.uk` where both reduce to `co.uk`), causing the full path to be shown for unrelated sites, exactly as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — Domain matching is asymmetric: a `forum.example.com` instance shows the path for `www.example.com/u`, but an `example.com` instance does not (`"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false), even though the intent is to treat the same domain the same way

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the “same domain” path-inclusion logic is asymmetric: it includes the path when the website host is a parent of the instance host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), and also when both have the same number of labels and share the same parent domain (e.g. `forums.example.com` vs `www.example.com`). But if the instance is `example.com` and the website is `www.example.com`, it falls into the final `else` and returns only `website_host` (since `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false), dropping the path. This is a concrete edge-case gap in the new domain-matching behavior, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s definitively incorrect for the intended UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — Port is ignored in the match and dropped from the display, so `http://example.com:8080/x` on an `example.com` instance renders as `example.com/x` (a different destination), and other-domain URLs lose the `:port` the old code showed

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the code uses `URI(website.to_s).host` (which omits any `:port`) and later returns `website_host` or `website_host + URI(...).path`, so a URL like `http://example.com:8080/x` will be displayed as `example.com/x` (port dropped). The previous client-side logic `website.split("/")[2]` would have displayed `example.com:8080`, so this diff introduces a verifiable regression in displayed website text (even though the actual link href in the template remains `model.website`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — The "complete URL path" drops the query string and fragment (`example.com/index.php?user=bob` renders as `example.com/index.php`), which can misrepresent the link target

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the displayed value is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several branches, which intentionally includes only `.path` and omits `.query` and `.fragment`. So a URL like `http://example.com/index.php?user=bob#x` would display as `example.com/index.php` even though the actual link target in the template remains `model.website` (full URL). This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/incompleteness in the new display logic rather than a functional break of the link itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — website_name is not in untrusted_attributes and include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` (so it is never called), so a TL0 user's website host/path is exposed to anonymous viewers via the new field and span even though `website` is withheld by restrict_user_fields

adjudication.rationale: The finding is partly incorrect: the diff *does* add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (so that part is false). However, the serializer defines `def include_website_name` without the conventional `?` suffix used for conditional attribute inclusion, so it will not be used as an include predicate (i.e., it won’t be called for conditional inclusion). That can cause `website_name` to be serialized whenever `website_name` is declared as an attribute, rather than being gated as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The sibling-subdomain check only compares labels after the first one, so hosts on a shared parent (e.g. evil.trydiscourse.com vs forum.trydiscourse.com, or IP 1.2.3.4 vs 5.2.3.4) are treated as same-site and show the attacker-chosen path as if it were an internal forum link

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the “sibling-subdomain” branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats two hosts as related if `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`, i.e., it only compares labels after the first one. That means `evil.trydiscourse.com` and `forum.trydiscourse.com` will match and the method will return `website_host + URI(...).path`, exposing the attacker-controlled path in the displayed `website_name` (similarly, IPs like `1.2.3.4` vs `5.2.3.4` match on `2.3.4`). This is a real logic flaw in the new display-name computation introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — The parent-domain suffix check accepts bare TLDs/public suffixes (e.g. website host `com` or `co.uk` for forum.example.com / forum.example.co.uk) as the "same domain" and shows the full attacker path

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the final branch treats any `website_host` that is a suffix of `discourse_host` as a parent domain match: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host`. This will also match bare TLDs/public suffix-like hosts (e.g. `website_host == "com"` with `discourse_host == "forum.example.com"`), causing the code to return `"com" + path` (full attacker-controlled path) instead of just the host. The diff adds this logic and there is no guard against public suffixes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — The display text keeps host+path but drops port, query and fragment, so it can differ from the real href (e.g. `example.com:8080/x` shows as `example.com/x`, and `example.com/login?redirect=https://evil` shows as `example.com/login`), which makes a same-host open-redirect or other-port link look like a trusted internal path

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the serializer builds display text as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` (or just `website_host`). This necessarily drops `port`, `query`, and `fragment` from the rendered text, while the template’s `<a href={{model.website}}>` uses the full URL. This is a real mismatch introduced by the diff (previous JS `split("/")[2]` would include the port in the displayed host), and it can make links appear more “internal/trusted” than they are (e.g., hiding `:8080` or redirect query params).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — The TL0/anonymous `untrusted_attributes` list was not extended with `website_name`, so the spec misses that `website_name` is serialized unguarded and leaks a TL0 user's website domain/path to anonymous viewers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly extends `untrusted_attributes` to include `:website_name` in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` (added right after `:website`). Therefore the claim that the list “was not extended” is contradicted by the shown changes, and the alleged TL0/anonymous leak via missing guarding is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so it is never invoked, and no spec asserts the `website_name` key is absent when the website is blank or nil, which would have caught the dead predicate.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` the conditional inclusion hook is defined as `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`). Discourse/ActiveModel::Serializer convention is `include_<attr>?` for attribute gating, so this predicate will not be called and will not control whether `:website_name` is serialized. The added specs only assert positive cases (when `website` is set) and do not cover the blank/nil case that would reveal the broken include hook.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The equal-label-count sibling branch (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com) has no test at all, including negative cases like a.co.uk vs b.co.uk that this branch wrongly treats as the same domain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including a specific sibling-subdomain branch: `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` with a `split('.')[1..-1]` comparison. The added specs cover (1) different domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), (2) exact same domain, and (3) instance is a subdomain of the website domain (`forums.example.com`). There is no test exercising the equal-label-count sibling case (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) nor any negative cases for the suffix-based comparison this branch uses. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap for newly introduced logic; the “wrongly treats a.co.uk vs b.co.uk as same” concern is plausible given the `split` approach, but the verifiable part from the diff is the missing coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — The rescue path and nil-host path (unparseable URL, scheme-less `example.com/user`, whitespace or invalid characters) are untested, so the `return if website_host.nil?` behavior is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that explicitly handles parsing failures (`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`) and then short-circuits with `return if website_host.nil?`. The added spec (`user_serializer_spec.rb`) only exercises a well-formed `http://example.com/user` URL and domain-comparison branches, but does not cover the nil-host/rescue path (e.g., scheme-less or invalid URLs). That makes the new edge-case behavior unverified, which is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — The reverse and variant cases are untested: website www.example.com or forum.example.com on an example.com instance, mixed-case hosts, and ports, which all fall to host-only output or a case-sensitive mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (host/path handling based on comparisons to `Discourse.current_hostname` using `==`, `split('.')`, and `ends_with?`). The accompanying spec only covers three cases (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`, exact match, and `forums.example.com` as a subdomain of `example.com`). It does not cover the “reverse” subdomain case (e.g., instance `example.com` with website `www.example.com`/`forum.example.com`), nor variants like mixed-case hostnames or hostnames with ports, which could change comparison outcomes because the code performs case-sensitive string comparisons and assumes comparable hostname formats. This is a concrete test/edge-case gap introduced by the new logic, not a demonstrable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:69 — All cases use a single URL shape (`/user` path), so trailing-slash, query-string/fragment dropping, and bare-root URLs are never asserted on the display output.

adjudication.rationale: The updated spec only sets `user.user_profile.website` to a single shape (`http://example.com/user`) and asserts `website_name` outcomes based on hostname comparisons. Given the new formatting logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` uses `URI(...).host` and appends only `URI(...).path` (ignoring query/fragment and not covering root or trailing-slash variants), the tests don’t exercise edge cases like `http://example.com/`, `http://example.com`, `.../user/`, or `.../user?x=1#y` that could affect displayed output. This is a concrete coverage gap for the newly added nontrivial logic, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — Replacing the reactive client-side `websiteName` with the static server field `model.website_name` has no JS/acceptance coverage, and `User#save` (models/user.js.es6:210) only syncs `bio_excerpt`, so after a website edit the profile shows a stale or missing website until reload.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace the client-side computed `websiteName` with `model.website_name` (template change) and adds a server-side `website_name` method plus serializer specs. However, the finding’s core claim—that after editing the website the UI will be stale because `User#save` only syncs `bio_excerpt`—references code/behavior (models/user.js.es6:210 and save response semantics) not shown in this diff, so the stale-after-edit defect is not verifiable from the provided changes. The diff also doesn’t establish that there is “no JS/acceptance coverage” globally, only that this PR adds serializer tests.
